title: Snow Family data transfer selection
scenario: Alderwick Museums Consortium must move 600 TB of digitised archive from storage arrays in one building into AWS within 30 days to meet a grant condition, and the IT head's draft plan is to order Snowball Edge appliances. AWS Snow Family (Snowball Edge, Snowcone and Snowmobile) is closed to new customers, so no device can be ordered and the plan must be replaced. The building's internet link is 500 Mbps and the carrier cannot raise it for at least 12 weeks. After the bulk load, the consortium expects about 400 GB of new scans each month. It holds an AWS Enterprise Support plan, and its staff can transport storage devices up to a five-hour drive.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
No AWS Snow Family device can be ordered, and the design record must state this status rather than present the option as current
Finance will not fund a faster internet circuit
Data must be verified as intact after it lands, and the monthly scans must not need another physical transfer
requiredArtifact: Architecture decision record + diagram notes + cost assumptions

rubric.label: Why live lab was unsuitable documented

The one-time 600 TB load finishes inside 30 days, the record shows the sustained rate required (about 1.85 Gbps) cannot be met over the existing 500 Mbps link, and it explains why the original appliance plan cannot be used
The roughly 400 GB of monthly scans reach AWS over the existing link with integrity verification and without another physical transfer

constraint_reason: Service unavailable or not disposable in a personal same-day lab
